summary: Iter31 — profile-picture upload bug fix + logo styling verification. All 19 backend pytest cases pass (100%): happy-path JPEG/WEBP, all 8 HEIF/HEIC ftyp brands (hvc1/heix/heim/heis/hevc/mif1/msf1/avif), garbage-base64 → 400, plain-text payload → 400, oversized >15MB → 400, missing-auth → 401, BOLA cross-user → 404, upload-batch happy-path (3 pics), batch BOLA → 404, batch no-auth → 401, and post-upload GET persistence verified. Frontend: Expo web preview bundles cleanly with the new expo-image-picker plugin + Android permission additions; auth-screen logo renders at exactly 140x140 with a transparent background (no white edges) as required. Picture upload pipeline is fully functional end-to-end.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 3920 lines — well above the 700-line guideline. Should be split into routers (auth, pictures, matches, tina, admin) for maintainability. Not blocking but worth tracking.

Two deprecation warnings observed in the web bundle: 'shadow* style props are deprecated, use boxShadow' and 'useNativeDriver not supported (web)'. These are React Native Web fallbacks, not blockers, but the shadow* warning is fixable by switching to boxShadow on the affected styles.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (logo size + transparent BG verified visually, bundle clean)

seed_data_creation: Created two test users via dev OTP flow: TEST_iter31_userA@example.com and TEST_iter31_userB@example.com (used for happy-path + BOLA tests).
context_for_next_testing_agent: All HEIF brand variants accepted as designed. require_owner returns 404 (not 403) by design — intentional to avoid leaking valid user_ids. Global auth gate at /api/* correctly returns 401 for missing Authorization on /user/pictures/*. The /user/pictures/upload endpoint correctly returns 400 with a friendly detail for invalid/oversized payloads instead of opaque 500s. Logo renders at 140x140 on auth screen with transparent BG (verified via mobile viewport screenshot at 390x844).
rca_of_issue: Original APK upload failures (user-reported 'Upload Failed. Failed to upload picture.') traced to two root causes: (1) backend MIME sniff in picture_service.py only matched the literal ASCII string 'ftypheic', so modern iPhone HEIF files using brands like hvc1/heix/heim/mif1 were rejected as 'unsupported MIME' (returned None → 500); (2) Android permission gap (READ_MEDIA_IMAGES + expo-image-picker plugin not in app.json) meant Android 13+ couldn't read the gallery at all. Both are fixed in the current build: backend now accepts every HEIF brand + AVIF, returns 400 (not 500) for bad input, and Android permissions/plugin config are in app.json. Verified via 8 parametrised HEIF tests, 3 error-path tests, and live web bundle check.
